seed: Objects of type `block` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [arm] show mixed outcomes: x x22, no_change x10, tags x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Crane/skewer mechanics: A1/A2 move ring+beam y-/+6, carrying blocks on the beam and pushing hit blocks in a chain; the whole move is cancelled if any block would leave y in [2,58].
A4/A3 change beam w by +/-6 (w from 1 to 43). If the next/collected block is hooked at x == beam.x+w-5, every block on the beam moves too; otherwise an extend pushes the blocks it sweeps over. A blocked group (x>48, x<0, or into the ring) means the beam changes alone.
The block-A3 hypothesis was a red herring: the outcome depends on whether a block is hooked and on ring blocking, not on click position. Clicks, A5 and A7 do nothing.
Tags: a hooked next block alone on the beam becomes collected and the rightmost todo becomes next. A collected block that is no longer hooked goes back to next, and the old next goes back to todo.
The program keeps no hidden state. Not observed: ring y bounds (guessed 0..58), tie-break between todo blocks with equal x, and a hooked extend with other blocks off the beam rows.
